claim: § Cross-Domain Resonance + The reframe: a toroidal wavetable and a Volterra kernel are one N-D field distinguished only by how it is read; a single control surface toggled between synth-scan and input-process is the monism made audible.

pieces.what: One stored 2D field with a button: scan-read by two phasors it is an oscillator, input-read by the input's own delayed samples it is an effect on a loop. Same table, two instruments.
pieces.walks_up_from: a 2D table read at one point

pieces.what: Feed two tones in and read the second-order kernel along its diagonal (Hammerstein: harmonics only) and then off it (intermodulation appears); a spectrum marks which products each slice keeps.
pieces.walks_up_from: one sine through a static waveshaper

pieces.what: Ring modulation as the bilinear slice, shown as the simplest input-read special case of the same field.
